current_date: Checklists dated 01.07.2025 and 15.05.2026 (in file names); hub page updated 17 August 2026
current_evidence: The council's 'Planning application checklist and submission' page (updated 17 Aug 2026) still links Major-Application-Checklist-01.07.2025.docx as the Major Applications checklist. It is one of 13 type-specific checklists on that page, and Householder, Variation and NMA were reissued on 15.05.2026.

issues.detail: The council has no single local list. It publishes 13 type-specific checklists: Householder, Full, Listed Building Consent, Advertisement, Outline (some/all matters reserved), Reserved Matters, Existing/Proposed Certificate of Lawfulness, Major, Change of Use, Variation and Non-material Amendment. Grokbot read only the Major and Full checklists and marked every other application type '(none)', even though a dedicated checklist exists for each.
issues.evidence: Checklist hub page 'Checklist for applicants' links 13 checklists, e.g. Listed-Building-Consent-Checklist-01.07.2025.docx and Variation-Application-Checklist-15.05.2026.pdf

issues.detail: Householder is marked '(none)', but the 15.05.2026 Householder checklist sets local requirements: Flood Risk Form where the site is in a flood risk area on EA maps or the council's strategic flood risk maps; Heritage Assessment where the site affects a conservation area or its setting, a listed building or its setting, a scheduled monument, archaeology or non-designated assets; a dropped kerb section to a recognised scale where a dropped kerb is proposed; and an existing block plan where a new access is proposed.
issues.evidence: Householder-Application-Checklist-15.05.2026.pdf: 'Flood Risk Form ... falls within a flood risk area on the Environment Agency maps and/or our local strategic flood risk maps'

issues.detail: Almost all rows come from the Major Application checklist but are filed under 'Full planning' with no distinction between major and minor full applications. For example, 'A sequential test is required for all major applications that falls within a flood risk zone', the Travel Plan, the S106 Heads of Terms and the Retail Impact Assessment are major-application items. Minor full applications have their own, shorter Full Application checklist.
issues.evidence: app_type_rows source = Major-Application-Checklist-01.07.2025.docx for all but the FRA row

issues.detail: Many trigger excerpts are cut-off fragments with no condition, and some lose the threshold. Examples: Air Quality 'require an Air Quality Assessment.'; Retail Impact 'square metres a Retail Impact Assessment must be submitted.' (floorspace figure missing); Transport 'In all other cases, a Transport Statement will suffice.'; Open space 'Children's play areas f.'; Block plan 'on the block plan.'; SCI 'the Council's Statement of Community Involvement.'; Waste 'any sustainable waste management.'; Archaeology 'surveys and/or archaeological evaluation.'

Some requirements are mislabelled. 'Schedule of works (listed building)' carries the Arboricultural Method Statement text. 'Advertisement drawings / illumination details' carries lighting-scheme text (luminance levels, lighting pools) from the major checklist, not advertisement content.
issues.evidence: Schedule of works row: 'Arboricultural method statement (AMS): This document must not only detail how the site will be developed...'

issues.detail: The two 'Submission rules' items are process text and the same sentence appears twice, once from each checklist: 'We encourage documents to be submitted electronically through the Planning Portal or via email to planning@nelincs.gov.uk.' The drawing-standard items (plain paper, north point, scale labelling) are general plan-quality notes, not local requirements.
issues.evidence: tab_items Submission rules (Full and Major checklist headers)

issues.detail: The list date comes from the upload-folder path. The checklist set now has mixed dates: the major and full checklists are dated 01.07.2025 in their file names, while Householder, Variation and NMA were reissued on 15.05.2026. The 'Planning page' field is only the council homepage (https://www.nelincs.gov.uk), not the checklist page.

summary: Grokbot's Major checklist link is current, but it is only one of 13 type-specific checklists. Grokbot ignored the rest (including the May 2026 Householder checklist with its flood and heritage requirements), filed major-only items under Full planning, and many of its triggers are cut-off fragments or mislabelled.

withdrawn_issues.detail: This audit could not read the text of the .docx checklists (Major, Full), because WebFetch returned binary data. The exact thresholds for the major-application items could therefore not be checked against the source, and the Householder PDF and the checklist hub page were checked instead.
withdrawn_issues.grok_comment: The DOCX checklists can be read. The raw copy of the Major Application checklist is about 21.7 KB of text ("Major Application for Planning Permission ..."), and the Full checklist is also present, so the major-application thresholds can be checked against the source.
withdrawn_issues.claude_response: Accepted. This was a note about what my helpers could not read, not a Grokbot error, so it is removed from the issue counts. The council stays on "Still to check by hand".

grok_review: Reviewed by Grok 5 Nov 2026; Claude responded to every disagreement the same day.
